findings.headline: Revenue STA programmes forecast £1.9m below budget (16.4% shortfall)
findings.detail: STA revenue budget of £11.444m is forecast at £9.567m, a variance of -£1.877m. Spatial Development Strategy shows the largest underspend at £1.554m (full allocation forecast at zero). Other variances include Local Remediation Acceleration Plans (£166k forecast at zero), Active Travel revenue (£83k forecast at zero), and Rewilding Programme (£75k forecast from £150k budget). Core services and operational programmes remain on forecast.
findings.matters: Revenue programme underspends indicate non-progression on strategic initiatives or budget constraints; the Spatial Development Strategy underspend is material as planning strategy underpins economic delivery
findings.figures: Revenue budget £11,444k, forecast £9,567k, variance -£1,877k. Spatial Development Strategy: £1,554k budgeted, £0 forecast. Local Remediation Plans: £166k budgeted, £0 forecast. Active Travel: £83k budgeted, £0 forecast. Rewilding: £150k budgeted, £75k forecast

findings.headline: Subject to Approval capital programmes forecast £44.3m below budget (58.7% shortfall)
findings.detail: The combined authority's STA capital budget for 2026/27 is £75.527m but Q1 forecasts only £31.234m expenditure, a variance of -£44.293m. Major contributors to the underspend include Bus Franchising Depot Improvements (£21m forecast at zero), Local Growth Plan Delivery Fund (£7.413m forecast at zero), Capital for Skills grant (£3.5m forecast at zero), Resilience Plan Capital Fund (£3.173m forecast at zero), and A10 Upgrade (£3m forecast at zero). Programmes remaining on forecast include transport operations, railway station development, and housing programmes.
findings.matters: Large forecast underspends indicate either delivery delays or grant funding shortfalls affecting capital deployment; finance directors assess capital delivery risk and lenders evaluate creditworthiness partly through infrastructure project delivery
findings.figures: Capital budget £75,527k, forecast £31,234k, variance -£44,293k. Bus Franchising Depot: £21,000k budgeted, £0 forecast. Local Growth Plan: £7,413k budgeted, £0 forecast. Capital for Skills: £3,500k budgeted, £0 forecast. Resilience Plan: £3,173k budgeted, £0 forecast. A10 Upgrade: £3,000k budgeted, £0 forecast

findings.headline: Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure capital programme reforecasted from £3.0m budget to £0.5m.
findings.detail: The Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure programme is forecast to deliver only £0.5m against a full-year budget of £3.0m, representing a £2.5m reduction (83% of budget). Year-to-date spend is £16k. Slippage of £2.5m is requested, indicating the authority expects to recover this in later quarters, but the scale of reforecasting suggests either a substantial delivery delay or programme rescoping.
findings.matters: A material downward revision of a transport decarbonisation capital scheme signals either delivery challenges or changed funding assumptions; the recovery trajectory needs monitoring.
findings.figures: Budget £3,000k; Forecast £500k; Variance -£2,500k; Requested Slippage £2,500k
findings.quote: Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure - 16 16 3,000 500 -2,500 -2,500 2,500

findings.headline: Investment income forecast at £8.9m, exceeding budget by £4.3m.
findings.detail: Investment income is forecast to deliver £8.9m against a budget of £4.7m, an upside of £4.3m (92% more than budgeted). Year-to-date actual of £2.4m in three months indicates an effective annual run rate of approximately £9.7m. This outperformance indicates either higher cash balances held by the authority or significantly better interest rates than assumed when the budget was set.
findings.matters: Better-than-expected investment returns strengthen the authority's financial position and support reserves without requiring spending reductions or operational income growth.
findings.figures: Budget £4,655k; Forecast £8,926k; Positive Variance £4,271k
findings.quote: Interest Receivable on Investments -2,433  -4,655 -8,926 -4,271  -4,271

findings.headline: Growth Hub export programme transferred to national DBT delivery, freeing £250k of local budget
findings.detail: The planned local delivery of the export programme under 'Team Cambridgeshire and Peterborough' is no longer required as it is now being delivered via the national programme run by the Department for Business and Trade. The £250k underspend will be returned to the general fund for use in the medium-term financial plan.
findings.matters: Changes to national programme delivery reduce local authority budget requirements and free resources for reallocation
findings.figures: Variance -£250k (Budget £789k, Forecast £539k)
findings.quote: This forecast underspend is due to the planned delivery of an export programme which is now being delivered via the national programme run by DBT. As locally funded delivery is no longer required, this budget will be returned to the general fund and considered within the overall setting of the medium-term financial plan

findings.headline: Resilience Plan Phase 2 and Health/Wellbeing Strategy development both deferred to 2027/28
findings.detail: The Resilience Plan has adopted a phased approach with Phase 1 commissioned and due to report in November 2026, while Phase 2 development is now scheduled for 2027/28. The Health/Wellbeing Strategy development was also deferred and is expected to complete in 2027/28, with current year spend focused on expert advice and system tools.
findings.matters: Significant programme slippage affects medium-term planning timelines and the phasing of capital allocation decisions
findings.figures: Resilience Plan variance -£300k, Health/Wellbeing Strategy variance -£300k (together £600k slippage)
findings.quote: Following decision by Growth Committee to take a phased approach to the Resilience Plan (with Phase 1 commissioned and due to report in November 2026) the Phase 2 development work will now take place in 2027/28

findings.headline: Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure programme defers £2.5m after DfT requires procurement process changes
findings.detail: The programme has revised its procurement process to meet Department for Transport expectations. Expenditure is now expected to commence from Q4 2026/27, with contract award anticipated during 2026/27. The remaining funding will be reprofiled across the subsequent three years.
findings.matters: Changes in government requirements for procurement delay major capital investment and shift funding across future years, affecting capital planning certainty
findings.figures: Variance -£2,500k (Budget £3,000k, Forecast £500k for 2026/27)
findings.quote: Following changes to the procurement process to meet the expectations of the DfT, expenditure is now expected to commence from Q4 2026/27.

findings.headline: A10 Upgrade programme defers £630k of expenditure pending government feedback on Major Road Network funding
findings.detail: The A10 programme has adopted a revised delivery profile, deferring elements of expenditure until receiving government feedback on the Major Road Network funding programme. The authority is continuing targeted activities to maintain momentum and preserve programme readiness.
findings.matters: Government funding decisions directly affect the timing and delivery of major capital projects, affecting both programme flow and funding certainty
findings.figures: Variance -£630k (Budget £1,259k, Forecast £629k for 2026/27)
findings.quote: The variance within the A10 programme is primarily due to a revised delivery profile while awaiting government feedback on the Major Road Network (MRN) funding programme.

findings.headline: Active Travel Officer post being advertised for third time as recruitment challenges delay Community Grant Scheme
findings.detail: The recruitment difficulty to the Active Travel Officer position is causing delays in the Community Grant Scheme delivery, with a £235,000 underspend. The position is currently being advertised for a third time, with expectation to successfully fill it during the current financial year.
findings.matters: Recruitment challenges delay service delivery and grant distribution, showing whether the authority can fill key posts to deliver programmes on time
findings.figures: £235,000 underspend in Community Grant Scheme; £551,000 total Active Travel programme variance
findings.quote: Delays in the delivery of the Community Grant Scheme have resulted in an underspend of £235,000. This is primarily due to the continued challenges in recruiting to the Active Travel Officer post, which is currently being advertised for a third time.

findings.headline: Youth Guarantee Trailblazer exceeded target with 146 young people engaged against 115-person target
findings.detail: Following recommissioning of core delivery partners, programme is performing strongly with 146 young people engaged against target of 115. All planned Year 2 commissioning activity completed with £1.5 million Interventions Fund awarded to 20 projects. Funding committed through 31 March 2027.
findings.matters: Shows strong program delivery and performance recovery after recommissioning. Exceeding targets indicates effective targeting and engagement. Committed funding through March 2027 provides spending visibility.
findings.figures: 146 engaged vs 115 target; £1.5 million fund; 20 projects commissioned; funding to 31 March 2027
findings.quote: Following the extension and recommissioning of core delivery partners during the first quarter of this financial year, the programme has continued to perform strongly, engaging 146 young people against a target of 115 for the period.

findings.headline: Impact assessment underway on £2 national bus fare cap extension to 31 December 2027
findings.detail: Government extended £2 cap on single bus fares outside London from original end date to 31 December 2027. Combined Authority is reviewing Tiger Pass scheme in this context, including financial and operational impacts. Findings will be reported to future Transport Committee and Board meetings once work concludes.
findings.matters: Government policy changes can create unexpected financial pressure or opportunity. Understanding implications for council-managed transport revenue is essential for budget planning.
findings.figures: £2 cap extended to 31 December 2027
findings.quote: Research is underway to assess the potential impact of this policy on passenger demand. The assessment will consider the implications for the Tiger Pass scheme, including financial and operational impacts.

findings.headline: £224 million homelessness funding approved with draft action plan due 1 December 2026
findings.detail: £224 million funding approved for homelessness work including support to end rough sleeping. For 2026/27, funding will be passported to Local Authorities with monitoring arrangements in place. Draft Homelessness Action Plan due 1 December 2026 will set framework for future spending and activity.
findings.matters: Represents significant new funding responsibility and budget area for the authority. Whether distributed through or managed by the authority, it creates financial and oversight obligations requiring budgeting and monitoring.
findings.figures: £224 million approved; draft plan deadline 1 December 2026
findings.quote: Funding of £224 million has been approved, with a key output being the development of a draft Homelessness Action Plan by 1 December 2026. This will provide the framework for future activity and investment, including additional funding to support the ambition to end rough sleeping.

findings.headline: £26.1 million Brownfield Land Fund Outline Business Case approved for housing delivery
findings.detail: Outline business case taken to Funding Committee for Brownfield Land Fund to support delivery of 870 homes. Approximately half of the £26.1m funding is profiled for year one. Homes supported must start on site by 2031.
findings.matters: Represents a significant capital investment program requiring financing and execution within defined timescale. Finance directors monitor capital deployment, funding requirements, and delivery progress.
findings.figures: £26.1 million programme; approximately £13m year one; 870 homes target; delivery by 2031
findings.quote: A Brownfield Land Fund Outline Business Case was taken to Funding Committee for a £26.1 million programme to support the delivery of 870 homes. Around half of the funding is profiled for year one, requiring the programme to move at pace and focus on deliverable sites.

findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation decision for Cambridgeshire and Peterborough paused and put under review
findings.detail: Secretary of State announced LGR decisions would be paused and reviewed. Decisions in four areas (Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk, Suffolk) were withdrawn entirely. Fourteen other areas, including Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, have decisions paused pending review. The Mayor and Officers continue working with government.
findings.matters: LGR decisions carry major financial implications including organizational restructuring, staffing changes, and service delivery redesign. Uncertainty about timing and outcome affects medium-term financial planning and creditworthiness.
findings.figures: 4 areas with decisions withdrawn; 14 areas paused including Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
findings.quote: Decisions in four areas were withdrawn, these included Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk; while fourteen other areas are to be reviewed and paused, this included Cambridgeshire and Peterborough.

findings.headline: Bloomberg Philanthropies programme securing circa £250k for data, digital and AI capacity over 18 months
findings.detail: Authority is tranche one of 18-month Bloomberg Philanthropies programme supporting Mayors and Strategic Authorities. Co-delivery through Inner Circle Consulting, London School of Economics, Public Digital and Portland Communications. Public Digital work specifically focused on enhancing data, digital and AI capabilities to support evidence-based decision making and delivery improvement. Anticipated £250k funding will support 2 FTE roles over 18-month period. Exact funding amount and mechanism to be confirmed.
findings.matters: External co-investment in strategic capability identified as area of organisational capacity and capability gap; demonstrates philanthropic interest in local government innovation and digital transformation; shows sector recognition of data and AI capability requirements.
findings.figures: Circa £250k funding (amount and mechanism pending confirmation); 2 FTE positions for 18-month period
findings.quote: It is anticipated that 2 FTE members of staff will be funded via Bloomberg Philanthropies for an 18 month period to support the Combined Authority drive forward a step change in data, digital and AI capabilities... This funding is anticipated to be circa £250k, with the exact amount and funding mechanism to be confirmed in the coming weeks.

findings.headline: MHCLG allocates £1.747m rough sleeping programme funding to authority for 2026/27, with provisional allocations for 2027-2029
findings.detail: MHCLG notification received 19 August 2026 allocating revenue funding for Rough Sleeping Programme for 2026/27, with provisional capital and revenue allocations for 2027/28 and 2028/29. Funding allocated across six local authorities using MHCLG Single Homelessness and Rough Sleeping formula, with largest allocations to Cambridge (£630,674) and Peterborough (£563,141). Provisional allocations: 2027/28 capital £1.423m, revenue £1.256m; 2028/29 capital £1.650m, revenue £1.270m.
findings.matters: New revenue stream devolved to authority; provides mechanism to deliver government commitment to end rough sleeping; creates multi-year funding visibility but also new governance, reporting and delivery accountability requirements for rough sleeping outcomes.
findings.figures: £1.747m 2026/27 allocation; provisional 2027/28 £1.423m capital and £1.256m revenue; provisional 2028/29 £1.650m capital and £1.270m revenue
findings.quote: On 19 August 2026 the Combined Authority received notification from MHCLG allocation of revenue funding for the Rough Sleeping Programme for 2026/27, with provisional revenue and capital allocations for 2027/28 and 2028/29.

findings.headline: Active Travel revenue programme underspending by £0.551m due to recruitment delays and programme delivery challenges
findings.detail: Forecast underspend of £0.551m on Active Travel Revenue Programme due to slippage into 2027/28. Root causes identified as challenges in recruitment to Active Travel Officer post and delays to Community Grant Scheme and Cycle Training programmes in Market Towns and Peterborough.
findings.matters: Reveals capacity constraints in delivering government-funded transport priorities; indicates staffing and HR challenges in specialist recruitment; demonstrates programme delivery risk in non-core service areas with specialist skill requirements.
findings.figures: £0.551m forecast underspend on Active Travel Revenue Programme
findings.quote: underspend of £0.551m on the Active Travel Revenue Programme which is due to slip into 2027/28 due to challenges in recruitment to the Active Travel Officer post along with delays to the Community Grant Scheme and Cycle Training programmes in Market Towns and Peterborough

findings.headline: £0.473m earmarked reserve drawdown approved for devolution response capacity
findings.detail: Board delegation approved for Chief Executive Officer to drawdown £0.473m from earmarked reserves for additional capacity to support response to government devolution agenda. Drawdown will only be made if required. Delegation also requested for Chief Finance Officer to include any future government capacity grant funding within authority budget if awarded.
findings.matters: Shows forward-looking response to government devolution agenda but creates reserve pressure if drawdown is needed; indicates recognition within finance function that forward resource investment is required ahead of formal funding confirmation; creates dependency on government delivering promised capacity grants.
findings.figures: £0.473m from earmarked reserves (set aside from previous underspending)
findings.quote: To delegate authority to the Chief Executive Officer to drawdown £0.473m from earmarked reserves for additional capacity to support the Authority's response to the Government's devolution agenda

findings.headline: Government devolution agenda will transfer substantial new responsibilities across multiple policy areas and governance functions
findings.detail: Government's 'Rewiring the State' agenda and authority's Established Mayoral Strategic Authority status confirmation signals significant acceleration in devolution. Proposed responsibility transfers include skills, employment support, transport, housing, planning, homelessness, fiscal devolution, public service integration, policing, fire governance and resilience, alongside enhanced accountability and governance requirements. Authority undertaking extensive preparatory work including policy development, capacity building, workforce planning, governance design and stakeholder engagement ahead of detailed funding confirmation.
findings.matters: Creates immediate and forward organisational capacity pressures and structural spending commitments; indicates multi-directorate implications and need for resource mobilization ahead of formal funding arrangements; represents strategic opportunity but also uncertainty about future cost and resource requirements.
findings.figures: Scope includes skills, employment support, transport, housing, planning, homelessness, fiscal devolution, public service integration, policing, fire governance and resilience; specific funding and implementation timeline not yet confirmed
findings.quote: The proposals would transfer substantial new responsibilities to Strategic Authorities across skills, employment support, transport, housing, planning, homelessness, fiscal devolution, public service integration, policing, fire governance and resilience

findings.headline: Treasury management income forecast to overachieve by £4.271m, driven by higher cash balances and interest rates
findings.detail: Treasury management income overachievement of £4.271m forecast. Driven by cash balances being higher than anticipated due to capital programme slippage and delays in spend, combined with new funding received in advance of expenditure. Additional overachievement reflects higher interest rates earned on liquidity balances than anticipated in budget.
findings.matters: Positive variance is contingent on capital slippage continuing; shows authority's cash management is benefiting from high interest rate environment but masks underlying capital programme underperformance; creates dependency on continued investment returns.
findings.figures: £4.271m overachievement of Treasury Management Income against budget
findings.quote: £4.271m overachievement of Treasury Management Income against budget. This increase in forecast is driven by a combination the Authority's cash balances being higher than anticipated due to delays in spend on the capital programme set out earlier in the outturn report, and new funding being received in advance of spend.

findings.headline: £1.741m revenue underspend forecast, predominantly due to timing rather than structural savings
findings.detail: Combined Authority forecasts full-year revenue outturn of £78.748m against budget of £80.489m. Underspend spread across Place and Economy (£912k underspend) and Transport (£843k underspend). Specific variances include £551k Active Travel slippage due to recruitment challenges, £300k Health and Wellbeing Strategy reprofiling, £300k Resilience Plan Phase 2 moved to 2027/28, and £250k Growth Hub underspend following transfer of export programme to national delivery.
findings.matters: Paper indicates variances expected to recover in latter quarters through timing catch-up rather than representing permanent savings; demonstrates revenue delivery is dependent on project acceleration and that early-quarter spend lags delivery partner claims profiles.
findings.figures: £1.741m revenue underspend forecast; Place and Economy -£912k, Transport -£843k, Active Travel -£551k, Health and Wellbeing -£300k, Resilience Phase 2 -£300k
findings.quote: the majority of service areas are forecasting to spend to budget

findings.headline: £48.150m of in-year capital budgets require rephasing into future years
findings.detail: Review of project budgets following 2025/26 slippage has identified material movements into future years. Key components include £21.000m for bus depots, £7.413m for Local Growth Fund delivery, £3.500m Skills Capital, and £3.173m Resilience Plan Capital. Majority of rephasing relates to budgets allocated to funds or schemes still requiring business case approval via the Single Assurance Framework, rather than in-delivery projects.
findings.matters: Shows extent of capital programme delays and uncommitted spending; indicates delivery acceleration will be required in latter quarters to meet annual targets and demonstrates reliance on SAF approval process for programme progression.
findings.figures: £48.150m capital rephasing (of £107.397m total capital budget); including £21.000m bus depots, £7.413m Local Growth Fund, £3.500m Skills Capital, £3.173m Resilience Plan Capital, £3.000m A10, £2.500m A141, £2.707m bus network improvements
findings.quote: £48.150m of the in-year capital budgets require rephasing. This includes both approved budgets and those that remain subject to approval.

findings.detail: The residual risk score declined from 14 through March 2026 to 10 by June 2026, suggesting an improved control environment and reduced likelihood of internal fraud.
findings.matters: Internal control quality signals organisational maturity to lenders; improved fraud controls indicate strengthened governance and reduced financial misstatement risk.
